builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning
summary: It replaces heuristic retrieval-then-concatenate memory selection (semantic similarity top-k) with a trained composer that jointly chooses which memories to include, how many, and in what order, using downstream task-success feedback rather than similarity scores. The cost is an additional trained policy and an RL training loop (ExPO/GRPO) that requires complete agent interactions per update, adding pipeline complexity, offline compute or API spend for rollouts, and a second model to maintain at inference. It can fail when the training distribution of tasks, executors, or memory banks shifts enough that the claimed transfer does not hold, and the RL signal can overfit to benchmark-style success metrics that do not match production objectives.
rationale: The idea directly addresses a real production failure mode (similarity-based retrieval selecting useless memories), but adoption requires RL training infrastructure and validation on the reader's own tasks before it can be justified over simpler retrieval heuristics.
technique: RL-trained memory assembly for LLM agents

claims.statement: It replaces heuristic retrieval-then-concatenate memory selection (semantic similarity top-k) with a trained composer that jointly chooses which memories to include, how many, and in what order, using downstream task-success feedback rather than similarity scores. The cost is an additional trained policy and an RL training loop (ExPO/GRPO) that requires complete agent interactions per update, adding pipeline complexity, offline compute or API spend for rollouts, and a second model to maintain at inference. It can fail when the training distribution of tasks, executors, or memory banks shifts enough that the claimed transfer does not hold, and the RL signal can overfit to benchmark-style success metrics that do not match production objectives.

Reports outperforming the strongest baseline for each of two frozen executors across three tau2-bench domains while reducing average memory-token usage by 16.9% and 4.9%; the learned policy is reported to transfer to unseen domains, executors, and memory banks.
